one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall inside the window: September/Q3 monthly revenue on ~Oct 8 and the Q3 earnings call with Q4 guidance on Oct 15 (quiet period Oct 5-14). July+August revenue already total NT$982B; Q3 guidance of $44.6-45.8B at 32 NT$/USD (~NT$1,427-1,466B) needs only ~NT$450-480B in September versus NT$515B in August, so a revenue beat at the top end or above is likely, and the chain (Nvidia guiding $108B, Broadcom guiding AI +236% YoY, Micron's Sept 30 beat-and-raise) argues for a firm Q4 guide and possibly early 2027 color (price hikes, capex). That is largely expected, though: the stock is within ~4% of its 52-week high and the Q3 gross-margin guide already dipped on N2/overseas dilution, so a margin or capex surprise can cut either way. I use a slight positive drift (median ~$465, +1.3%) and monthly vol ~11.5-12% (40%/3.5, a bit wider for the earnings event).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E on 2028 EPS (est. $26.5/ADR x 20x = $530, weight 0.6) and on 2027 consensus EPS ($22.4/ADR x 22x = $493, weight 0.4); blended ~$515.

thesis_break_reason: $320 (~30% below today, ~14x 2027 consensus EPS) would be below where the stock traded before the July guidance raise and would likely mean consensus 2027 EPS is being cut, i.e. a real AI-capex pullback by hyperscalers/Nvidia/Broadcom, a loss of leading-edge share to Intel 14A or Samsung, punitive tariffs outside the Taiwan carve-out, or a Taiwan Strait escalation, rather than ordinary 40%-vol noise.

reasoning: Industry evidence is uniformly strong for the next 12 months: TSMC holds a record 72.5% foundry share (TrendForce Q2); Nvidia grew revenue 106% and guides $108B; Broadcom says it has secured supply to double AI revenue to ~$115B in 2027; ASML is nearly sold out of Low-NA EUV for 2027 and adding 30% capacity; Micron's HBM for 2027 is contracted at higher prices; S&P projects hyperscaler capex rising ~50% to $1.3T in 2027; and TSMC has reportedly notified customers of 3-6% (advanced-node higher) price hikes from Jan 2027 with HPC surcharges. Against that: Q3 margin guidance dipped on N2 and overseas fab dilution, CoWoS shortage narrows into 2027, IDC sees smartphone/PC units flat in 2027 after a ~11-13% 2026 drop from memory costs, rivals (Intel 14A with Tesla, Samsung 2nm) are gaining credible second-source wins, and hyperscaler FCF is turning negative, which is the main bear mechanism. The stock at $459 is ~20.5x 2027 consensus ($22.4/ADR) and has run +64% in a year, so much good news is priced. My fair value of ~$515 (P/E on 2028/2027 EPS) gives ~+12% expected drift; consensus PT $552 is a bit higher. I built the ladder as a lognormal with median ~$510 and sigma 0.36 (slightly below the 40% realized vol, since TSM is a mega-cap) mixed with a 5% crash component (median ~$210) for a Taiwan or AI-bust tail informed by Polymarket's ~12-13% invasion-by-end-2027 odds (I treat a market-moving disruption inside the window as ~4-5%). That yields P(>=459) ~0.59 and P(>=551) ~0.40. Scenario mean (~$516) is consistent with the fair value. Research was limited to web search/fetch; no option data was consulted; X posts were not fetched.
